title: The integers are a G-ring
statement: The ring $\mathbf Z$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] (Stacks Project, More on Algebra, Proposition Tag 07PX, item (3)).

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition 07PX (tag 07PX, label proposition-ubiquity-G-ring, line 12652), item (3), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07PX; the proof states that the claim for $\mathbf Z$ follows from the definition and the fact that the completion of a discrete valuation ring is a discrete valuation ring. Proposition 07PX separately cites Proposition 07PS (tag 07PS) for its complete-local-ring item (2).

proof.text: The ring $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian, and its prime localizations are the field $\mathbf Q$ at $(0)$ and discrete valuation rings at the nonzero primes, by [lem-weil-pbc-z-localizations-dvr]. Thus the definition of a G-ring reduces the claim to checking regularity of the completion map at the field localization and at each DVR localization.

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition 07PX (tag 07PX), proof of item (3), first sentence: fields, Z and characteristic-zero Dedekind domains are handled from the definition; the localization description is the Dedekind criterion in Algebra Lemma 034X (tag 034X).

proof.text: At the zero prime, $\mathbf Z_{(0)}=\mathbf Q$ is a field, its maximal ideal is zero, and its completion is itself. The identity map of a field is flat and has the field as its only fibre; the fibre is a regular ring by [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring], so the identity map is regular by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition 07PX (tag 07PX), proof of item (3), the field case in the sentence preceding the itemized conclusion.

proof.text: For every nonzero prime ideal $(p)$, the localization $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ is a Noetherian local discrete valuation ring whose fraction field is $\mathbf Q$, hence has characteristic zero. Therefore the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-completion-regular] applies, and its completion map is regular. More explicitly, the completion is a discrete valuation ring by More on Algebra Lemma Tag 0AP1, completion is flat by Algebra Lemma Tag 00MB, its generic fibre $\operatorname{Frac}(\mathbf Z_{(p)}^\wedge)=\mathbf Q_p$ is geometrically regular over $\mathbf Q$ by characteristic zero, and its closed fibre is the field $\mathbf F_p$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition 07PX (tag 07PX), proof of item (3), together with Lemma Tag 0AP1 (completion-dvr), Algebra Lemma Tag 00MB (completion-flat), and Definition Tag 07BZ (regular ring map).

proof.text: The zero-prime and nonzero-prime cases cover every prime of $\mathbf Z$, so all localization-to-completion maps required by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] are regular. Therefore $\mathbf Z$ is a G-ring.

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition 07PX (tag 07PX), proof of item (3).
